key_findings.value: Equiaxed austenite grains with straight annealing twins and sparse dark particles; essentially single phase (no B2, consistent with the B2-free grade).

purpose.value: Microstructural observation of the as-cast plus homogenised 28Mn0Ni alloy sample (shown in Fig. 1a).

source.reason: Optical microscopy was performed with an Olympus optical microscope (section 2.3), and Fig. 1(a)/(b) present the as-cast plus homogenised and hot-rolled micrographs of 28Mn0Ni - panel (a) belongs to the as-homogenised sample.

processing_steps_notes.value: Three austenitic LDS grades (including the Ni-free 28Mn0Ni / Fe-28Mn-9Al-0.9C) were prepared by vacuum induction melting; the ingot weighed 30 kg. This is the as-cast part of the 'as-cast plus homogenised' condition.

source.reason: The paper states the three LDS grades (this being the Ni-free Fe-28Mn-9Al-0.9C / 28Mn0Ni grade) were prepared by vacuum induction melting to produce 30 kg ingots; this is the casting stage of the as-cast plus homogenised sample.

processing_steps_notes.value: The defect-free portions of the 30 kg as-cast ingots were homogenised at 1423 K for two hours. This is the homogenisation stage of the as-cast plus homogenised (as-homogenised) condition of 28Mn0Ni; the sample is the precursor/starting condition prior to hot rolling at 1323 K.

source.reason: Explicit statement that the defect-free portions of the 30 kg ingots were homogenised at 1423 K for two hours, and that Fig. 1(a,b) presents the as-cast plus homogenised condition of 28Mn0Ni - this defines the sample's process.
Fig. 1(a) optical micrograph of the as-cast plus homogenised 28Mn0Ni is described as equiaxed austenite grains with straight annealing twins and sparse dark particles.

Fig. 1(a) (as-cast plus homogenised 28Mn0Ni) is described as equiaxed austenite grains, and the text states the 28Mn0Ni alloy in the as-cast plus homogenised condition is primarily made of a single phase, whereas the Ni-containing alloys are two-phase.
Overall as-cast plus homogenised microstructure of the Ni-free 28Mn0Ni alloy taken from the text and the Fig. 1(a) description.

overall_structure.value: As-cast plus homogenised 28Mn0Ni alloy: primarily made of a single phase - equiaxed austenite (γ) grains containing straight annealing twins and sparse dark particles; essentially a single-phase austenitic structure (no B2, this being the B2-free grade).

source.reason: The only microstructural description pertaining to the as-cast plus homogenised 28Mn0Ni condition is given in section 3.1 and Fig. 1(a); the grain-size / phase-fraction / twin-fraction values reported in Table 2 are for the hot-rolled condition and are therefore not attributed to this sample.

unmapped_findings: Chemical composition of the homogenised 28Mn0Ni (Fe-28Mn-9Al-0.9C) ingot in wt% (Table 1, analysed by wet chemical method/standard emission spectroscopy): Mn 28.3, Al 9.0, C 0.9, Ni not added (-), Fe balance. This is the analysed composition of the homogenised ingot from which this sample is taken.

28Mn0Ni is the Ni-free, B2-free grade of the study; its as-cast plus homogenised microstructure is primarily a single phase (austenite), in contrast to the Ni-containing 28Mn5Ni and 15Mn5Ni grades which are two-phase in the same condition.

This as-homogenised 28Mn0Ni ingot is the precursor/starting condition prior to hot rolling (hot rolling was subsequently carried out at 1323 K with ~85% total thickness reduction and ~15% reduction per pass); the mechanical properties, phase fractions and TEM/EBSD data reported elsewhere in the paper are for the hot-rolled condition and therefore do not apply to this as-homogenised sample.
